studies.design: Randomized online four-condition experiment; 6-minute birdsong or traffic soundscapes of low/high diversity.
studies.outcome: Anxiety and paranoia declined in both birdsong groups; no cognitive improvement.
studies.limitations: Acute outcomes; no neutral-sound control; not migraine or pain; no clear diversity advantage.
studies.audio_access: Four exact study MP3s publicly downloadable from OSF; repository audio license unspecified.

studies.population: 174 randomized, 173 analyzed adults with acute migraine (body counts; abstract inconsistently says183).
studies.design: Open-label ER trial: patient-chosen music plus usual medication versus usual medication alone.
studies.outcome: At1hour, >=3-point pain reduction in82/87 vs73/86 (94%vs85%;p=.037). Meanpain2.63vs3.40(p=.0173).
studies.limitations: No active auditory control; varied concurrent medication; one music participant withdrew after irritation/worsening. Abstract headache-free wording conflicts with body score0–2 definition. No frequency isolation.
studies.audio_access: No exact open playlist or stimuli identified; participant-chosen genres. Data on request.
studies.citation: Diamante PAB, Roxas AA Jr. Annals of Headache Medicine2020;04:01. doi:10.30756/ahmj.2020.04.01
studies.stimulus_detail: At least30minutes of shuffled music from preferred-genre lists(classical,pop,rock,jazz,R&B,meditation,religious,OPM); tracks not individually reported.

studies.population: 78 adolescents with migraine or tension-type headache
studies.design: Randomized attention-placebo-controlled trial: six music-therapy sessions over8weeks versus rhythm-pedagogy sessions.
studies.outcome: Neither treatment superior; both showed about20% mean headache-frequency reduction.
studies.limitations: Therapist intervention, not passive listening; mixed primary headache diagnoses.
studies.audio_access: No open standardized audio stimulus dataset identified.

studies.design: Laboratory mental-arithmetic stressor followed by nature or environmental-noise sound conditions.
studies.outcome: Skin-conductance recovery tended to be faster for nature; high-frequency heart-rate variability showed no effect.
studies.limitations: Physiological stress recovery is not migraine efficacy; small laboratory sample.
studies.audio_access: No verified openly licensed exact stimulus files located in this search.

studies.design: Preregistered counterbalanced fMRI experiment with matched audiovisual nature, urban and indoor environments during electrical pain.
studies.outcome: Pooled pain ratings lower for nature than urban (difference-.54on0–8scale) and indoor(-.48); nociception-related neural responses also reduced.
studies.limitations: Combined visual+audio intervention; cannot attribute effect to sound or a frequency band; experimentally induced pain, not migraine.
studies.audio_access: Behavioral/fMRI-derived data and analysis onOSF; exact reusable audio not confirmed.
